newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia trims spending, income in '97 budget plan.
newsitem.headline: Russia trims spending, income in '97 budget plan.

text.p: The Russian government shaved one trillion roubles from income and from expenditure in a new 1997 budget draft which also increased finance for the poor and for the military and industry.

Russian news agencies said the government decided to cut planned revenues to 432.8 trillion roubles from 433.64 trillion in the first draft and to trim expenditures to 523.5 trillion roubles from 524.34 trillion.

First Deputy Finance Minister Vladimir Petrov told a cabinet meeting that social spending would rise, although the budget deficit would remain unchanged at 3.3 percent of gross domestic product, or 90.70 trillion roubles.
He gave no details of where the extra funding for the social sector would come from.
The State Duma lower house of parliament sent a draft 1997 budget back to the government earlier this month, criticising unrealistically high revenue plans.
Interfax news agency quoted Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin as saying that the government would send the new draft budget to parliament at the weekend.

Chernomyrdin said the cabinet should provide adequate finance for agriculture, industry and the social sphere. He said the government should first support firms making competitive goods and then outline a policy towards unprofitable firms.
Many ministers are worried at a persistent slump in Russian industrial production. Jan-Sept output was 5.5 percent lower than for the same period of 1995.
The draft 1997 budget assumes a slim one percent growth in industrial output.
The fall in industrial production and falling tax revenues result in pension and wage arrears which increase social tension in Russia. "People can no longer wait," Chernomyrdin said.
Meeting budget plans is a key element in talks between Russia and the International Monetary Fund about whether to release monthly tranches of a $10 billion three-year loan.
